quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:

options.text: A deaf person.
A person involved with a traffic study.
A blind person.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A blind person.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to a pedestrian who is blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: As you near an intersection, the traffic light changes from green to yellow. Your best action is to:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Apply the brakes sharply to stop.
Be prepared to stop in the center of the intersection.
Be prepared to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Get ready to stop before you reach the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Steep downgrade.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead. Slow down to protect your brakes and avoid accidents.

questions.question: Fog can greatly reduce the visibility of other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Drive cautiously and reduce your speed.
Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to better illuminate the road and objects.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In fog, drive slowly and carefully. Do not use high beams. Use low beams instead—they work better in foggy conditions and help you see the road and objects ahead.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other:

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: With two railroad tracks, a second train may be coming on the other track. Wait until you see no train approaching on either track before you cross.

questions.question: An approaching driver fails to dim their high beam headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the bright lights and lets you stay on your path until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: When faced with an oncoming car to the left and a bicyclist to the right, you should:

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Split the difference.
Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: Deal with one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicyclist. Never try to squeeze between two hazards at the same time.

questions.question: Highway signs that inform drivers about hazardous conditions are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell you about dangerous conditions ahead. Obey them for your safety. Ignoring a warning sign can lead to accidents.

questions.question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes:

options.text: In curves and on hills.
Next to churches and schools.
At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
On freeway on-ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are white lines at intersections and crosswalks. They show where you must stop.

questions.question: You approach an emergency vehicle that is stopped with its lights flashing. You must:

options.text: Slow down. If possible, change lanes so you will not drive next to the stopped emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and continue to drive at the same speed.
Accelerate to quickly pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If possible, change lanes so you will not drive next to the stopped emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow down and change lanes away from the stopped emergency vehicle if it is safe. If you cannot change lanes, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible.

questions.question: You are stopped in a line of vehicles at a stop sign. After the vehicles ahead pass through and there is no cross traffic, you:

options.text: May go through the intersection without stopping again.
Must stop at the stop sign or stop line before going.
May slowly roll past the stop sign.
May follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop at the stop sign or stop line before going.
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at a stop sign before proceeding. Check for traffic before moving forward. Do not skip the stop just because other vehicles are around you.

questions.question: You may drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road:

options.text: As long as you are not the driver.
If you sit in the back seat.
If you sit in the back of a pickup truck.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or carry open alcohol in a vehicle on any public road. You cannot have an open alcohol container anywhere in the car, including the back seat or truck bed.

questions.question: When driving, you must stop your vehicle:

options.text: At a stop sign.
At a red light.
When a police officer tells you to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop in these situations: at a stop sign, at a red light, or whenever a police officer signals you to stop.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The divided highway is ending.
One-way traffic ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Stay to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay to the right side of the divider ahead.

questions.question: You cannot pass on either side of a ____ center line.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no one can pass from either direction. This line separates traffic moving in opposite directions on a two-way road.

questions.question: When stopped by police or at an equipment check, you must show:

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Your driver's license.
Proof of vehicle registration.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must have your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in the vehicle at all times. You must show all three when asked by police.

questions.question: When you see a green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Go through, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: You may go through on a green light if the intersection is clear. Yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection. Slow down as needed in case the light changes.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, you should:

options.text: Turn off all lights.
Use only parking lights.
Use only headlights.
Turn on emergency flashers and low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: At night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on. This helps other drivers see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, you should:

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before going.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go as soon as the train passes.
Go when you see one clear track.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before going.
questions.explanation: Do not cross until you can see all tracks are clear. Another train may be coming on a different track. Even if one train passes, check all tracks before proceeding.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold medicine
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair driving, including illegal drugs and over-the-counter or prescription medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, a small vehicle driver should be prepared for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Extra air pollution.
Wind gusts from the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles sideways. Small vehicle drivers should be ready to steer carefully when passing large vehicles going fast.

questions.question: To turn left on a multilane, one-way street or highway, start from:

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:

options.text: Traffic lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how quickly you can stop. Slow down on slippery or poor roads to stay in control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road:

options.text: You cannot see without turning your head.
Directly behind your vehicle.
You see in your rearview mirror.
You see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep downhill grade ahead.
Winding road.
Merging traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downhill grade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: The "No zone" is:

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
A special speed zone.
A roadway that restricts vehicle stereo volume.
The television show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have large blind spots on each side, in the rear, and in the front. Cars cannot be seen in these areas, which are called the "No zone."

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment:

options.text: Beer has less effect than wine.
Wine has less effect than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks have the most effect.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your bloodstream.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol hurts your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter. Only the total amount of alcohol in your blood affects you.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks should be given the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where it is safe to cross. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: To avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Never rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a highway, turn into or out of a driveway, or make a U-turn where allowed.

questions.question: What should you do when you meet an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them.
Show them you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and try to create distance between your vehicle and theirs. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers in that lane may make the movement the arrow shows, if they want to.
Drivers in that lane must make the movement the arrow shows, but only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers in that lane must always stop before making the movement the arrow shows.
Drivers in that lane must make the movement the arrow shows while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in that lane must make the movement the arrow shows while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the pavement tells drivers in that lane they must move in the direction the arrow points. Always follow traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction the arrow indicates.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look out the back window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the back window.
questions.explanation: Check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to see through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway begins.
Divided highway ends.
Bumps in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Stop next to the car in front of the space you want.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop next to the car in front of the space you want.
questions.explanation: After you find a space, check traffic, and signal, stop parallel to the car in front of the space you want. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive when conditions are dangerous.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive when conditions are good.
The suggested speed to drive when conditions are good.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive when conditions are good.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can drive when conditions are good. You can drive slower than the limit, but not faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, and when weather or road conditions are bad.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force your vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and steer back onto the road slowly.
Press hard on the brakes and stop.
Slow down by gently braking and turn the wheel to get back on the road safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by gently braking and turn the wheel to get back on the road safely.
questions.explanation: Keep driving with the wheels off the pavement and slow down by gently pressing the brakes. When you are going slow enough, turn the wheel to return to the road. Do not sharply turn the wheel to force your vehicle back onto the pavement.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires work less well.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
The road gets more slippery as you slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires work less well.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on wet roads, the less well your tires can remove water. If you go too fast, your tires lose grip and you hydroplane (slide on a layer of water).

questions.question: You are driving so slowly that cars are backing up behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.
Use your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. On a two-lane road, if you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up, pull off the road to let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road or weather conditions require it.
